agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager would see a candidly ordinary teacher letter. It leaves out the signed training records, the two clean state audits and the cut from 20 to 12 hours, which are the facts most likely to earn a phone screen.

honest.reason: The letter rightly drops the unsupported claim about halving training time, but it adds things the brief doesn't support: an annual revision cycle 'based on where new staff struggled', the claim 'I learn new systems quickly', and the topics the training supposedly covers.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are left raw: the letter never turns 20 to 12 hours into a 40% cut, never names the 17-point AP gain, and never adds up roughly 24 hours a year of adult training, so the strongest true forms are lost.

right_comparison.reason: The key before-and-after, onboarding cut from 20 hours to 12, is missing, so the letter never shows what training looked like before Laura changed it; only the AP 41% baseline appears.

qualification.reason: The GMP gap is hedged with a vague 'I plan to learn… thoroughly and early' instead of the enrolled course ending May 2, and the June 14 start constraint and interview availability are left out.

objections.reason: The letter admits the regulated-industry gap but doesn't answer it with the evidence the facts provide: signed training records for every trainee, two clean state audits and a GMP course already underway.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter as asked, but it is full of placeholders even though the name, the company (Calder Pharmaceuticals, Westfield) and the addressee (Karen Doyle) were known.
